narrative:
**Engagement cooled across the board this week, even as the four-week trend stayed positive.** Model downloads fell 6.9% week over week to 3.57M (from roughly 3.84M) across 25,742 tracked models, though they remained 12.5% above the four-week-ago level. Likes declined in parallel: model likes dropped 7.1% to 11,204 (-3.3% over four weeks) and Space likes fell 15.7% to 1,018 (-2.3% over four weeks), the steepest single-week move in the engagement cut. The simultaneous decline in all three measures suggests a broad activity dip rather than a shift between surfaces, but with only one- and four-week comparisons available (no 12-week baselines in this data), it is too early to separate a trend from normal week-to-week variance.

**On the model side, the story was reclassification as much as adoption.** The "other-open" family fell 35.2% to 5,652 models while "unknown" rose 17.0% to 11,840 — that unknown bucket now accounts for 46% of the 25,742 tracked models, so all family-level shares should be read as provisional. Among identified families, Qwen held steady at 5,537 (+1.3%) and Llama rose 3.9% to 1,059, while DeepSeek gained 38.5% to 428 and GLM/Zhipu 24.1% to 98; Kimi/Moonshot rose from 37 to 56, a small base where the percentage is directionally real but noisy. Gemma fell 8.9% to 763 and NVIDIA Nemotron 14.8% to 179. Within use cases, Qwen extended its lead in coding to 38.8% share (of 139 classified coding Spaces, +19.6%) and held 27.9% in chat-assistant (577 Spaces), where proprietary-API usage slipped 17.2% to 9.9%. Several use-case families sit on bases of 24–60 Spaces (robotics, education, music-generation, 3d-gaming), so week-over-week swings there are not reliable signals.

**Spaces told a more constructive story, led by scientific tooling.** Scientific-tools Spaces jumped 40.2% to 345 of 7,134 (coverage 1.0, i.e., full), lifting their share 36.0% to 4.84%, and the scientific-research vertical rose 16.8% to 9.28% penetration. Video-generation Spaces climbed 18.9% to 384 and voice-audio 5.8% to 418, while chat-assistant Spaces fell 5.3% to 1,018 and document-AI 4.3% to 443. By SDK, static Spaces grew 6.9% to 4,207 and Docker 10.5% to 619, while Gradio fell 4.6% to 2,191. Technology tags showed fine-tuned (+11.8% to 3.60%) and multimodal (+11.8% to 5.82%) gaining, against declines in local-inference (-23.9% to 2.40%), RAG (-14.7%) and tool-use (-10.9%); the legal vertical fell 31.4% to 0.98% off a thin base. Next week, watch whether the scientific-tools and video-generation surges in Spaces persist or revert, and whether the shrinking "other-open" / growing "unknown" model split is a genuine composition shift or a classification artifact that will correct.
